 Order

This petition under Section 438 of Cr.P.C. is filed by accused No.1 to enlarge him on bail in SC No.57/2023 pending on the file of V Additional Sessions Judge, Mysuru, arising out of Cr.No.138/2022 of Hullahalli Police Station, Mysuru.

2. FIR was registered against the petitioner, his parents and sisters for the offence punishable under Sections 304B, 302, 498A, 114 r/w 34 of IPC, on a complaint lodged by the mother of the deceased.
While filing charge sheet, the names of accused Nos.2 to 5 mentioned in the FIR have been deleted and one Suresha H.P. has been arraigned as accused No.2.

Charge is filed for the offences punishable under Sections 306, 498A r/w 34 IPC.
3.
In a nutshell, case of the prosecution is that deceased Mamatha was given in marriage to the petitioner on 26.03.2021 and at the time of marriage, he was given a dowry of Rs.1.50 lakhs.
After the marriage, the deceased was being subjected to cruelty by the petitioner.
He was making allegations against the deceased that her character is not good and he was picking up quarrel unnecessarily and giving physical and mental torture to her.

Further, on 30.08.2022 at about 12.30 p.m. accused No.2 came near the house of the deceased and told her that she is having illicit relationship with a boy from Jaipur and that he will disclose the same to her husband and others.
Unable to tolerate the physical and mental torture given by accused Nos.1 and 2, she committed suicide on the same day at about 5.30 p.m. by hanging herself.
3. The material on record would disclose that the deceased was staying in the house of her parents at the time of incident and even the petitioner was staying in the said house.
In the complaint lodged by the victim's mother she suspected that the petitioner, his parents and sisters by torturing her daughter, committed her murder.
However, while filing the charge sheet, the names of the parents and sisters of the petitioner have been dropped.

As per the charge sheet material, on 30.08.2022 i.e., on the date of incident accused No.2 came near the house of the deceased and started making allegations against her that she has illicit relationship with a person from Jaipur and that he will disclose the same to his husband and others.
4. It is the contention of the learned counsel for the petitioner that there are no allegations that this petitioner that he has either abetted or intentionally aided the deceased to commit suicide.

He contends, there are no allegations made against him that on the date of incident he has harassed the Premchand Naik vs The State Of Karnataka on 2 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/188657527/
2 deceased in any manner.

sentences.text: 5. The prosecution has to establish that the petitioner has either by his conduct or by any act has aided or abetted the deceased to commit suicide.
The ingredients of the offences alleged against the petitioner has to be established during trial.
Petitioner is in judicial custody since 25.09.2022.
Investigation is completed and charge sheet has been filed.

Hence, by imposing conditions,
petitioner can be enlarged on bail.

Accordingly, the following:
ORDER i. Petition is allowed.
ii.

The petitioner/accused No.1 shall be released in the event of his arrest in SC No.57/2023 pending on the file of V Additional Sessions Judge, Mysuru, arising out of Cr.No.138/2022 of Hullahalli Police Station, Mysuru, subject to following conditions:
( 1) Petitioner/accused No.1 shall appear before the Investigation Officer and shall execute a personal bond in a sum of Rs.1,00,000/- [Rupees one lakh only] with two sureties for likesum.
(2) Petitioner shall cooperate with the investigation and he shall not tamper with the prosecution witnesses in any manner.
(3) Petitioner shall furnish proof of his residential address and shall inform the Investigation Officer/Court regarding change in the address, if any.
(4) Petitioner shall regularly attend the Court proceedings.
